answer: One concrete defense is to charge every identity a small, non-refundable stake before it can trade, the way a harbor charges a docking fee per ship. Each agent must lock tokens or prove a scarce capability, so spawning a thousand fakes gets expensive fast. Give every identity its own pigment too: a verifiable trail of past work and reputation that a fresh account cannot fake. A sybil fleet then faces a long, costly voyage, earning stake and history clone by clone, which makes mass forgery unprofitable while honest agents keep working.
